# Remote Work Benchmarks for 2026

Hybrid work has settled into a stable pattern for most knowledge-work employers. Our annual benchmark study tracks policies at more than four hundred organisations, looking at how many remote days are permitted, what support is offered and how companies measure success.

## Remote days

The most common arrangement is now a fixed number of office days per week, usually agreed at team level. Fully flexible policies are still popular with smaller firms, while large enterprises tend to prefer formal limits that are reviewed regularly.

FACT: The median company in the 2026 study allows 2 remote days per week.
FACT: 41 percent of surveyed companies pay a home office stipend.
FACT: The average stipend among paying companies was 420 dollars per year.

## Core hours

Roughly half of employers define core hours during which staff must be reachable. Companies with core hours reported fewer scheduling conflicts, but employees in distributed teams said rigid windows made collaboration across time zones harder.

## Measuring success

Employers increasingly measure hybrid success by retention and engagement rather than office attendance. Organisations that combined clear expectations with practical support, such as stipends and good equipment, reported the highest satisfaction scores in our survey.

## Outlook

We expect policies to keep converging toward a two or three day office pattern, with more emphasis on intentional in-person time such as planning sessions, onboarding weeks and team celebrations. Companies that communicate the purpose of office days clearly tend to see better attendance without strict enforcement.
